name: Juglans

study_strategy.warning: Central Texas intermediates are documented. Do not ID a difficult tree from leaflet count alone; fruit/nut size and shell sculpture are higher-value.

quick_split: J. microcarpa — many narrow leaflets + tiny fruit/nut.
J. major — fewer/broader leaflets + medium fruit with smoother shell surface between grooves.
J. nigra — very large fruit + coarsely warty shell between deep grooves + large-tree habit.
comparison_lesson.caveat: FNA notes hybrid/intermediate material among central Texas walnut species; atypical individuals may not key cleanly from one character.

look_here_first: First verify walnut family: ALTERNATE PINNATELY COMPOUND leaf (separate leaflets along central rachis), a husked fruit, and when safely available a fallen twig showing CHAMBERED PITH. Then find mature fruit and (if legally and safely available) the cleaned hard NUT. Fruit diameter and the nut shell's raised/grooved texture distinguish these better than leaflet count alone; photograph fruit beside a ruler. A leaf-only ID may remain Juglans sp.

shared_genus_pattern.recognition: Deciduous native walnuts with alternate pinnately compound leaves, unisexual flowers, pendent staminate catkins, husked nuts and chambered twig pith.
shared_genus_pattern.terms: RACHIS = main axis carrying leaflets; HUSK = green covering outside hard nut; SCULPTURE = grooves, ridges and warts on cleaned shell; CHAMBERED PITH = cross-walled interior of a twig; STAMINATE = pollen-producing male flowers.
shared_genus_pattern.caution: Do not confuse an entire compound leaf with a single leaflet; do not mistake uncleaned husk texture for hard shell sculpture.

comparison_matrix.microcarpa: ~1.1–1.7 cm, longitudinally grooved, comparatively smooth between grooves
comparison_matrix.major: ~1.8–2.7 cm, deeply longitudinally grooved, comparatively smooth between grooves
comparison_matrix.nigra: ~3–4 cm, deep grooves with conspicuously rough/warty sculpture between
usually 15–19, sometimes 9–23; terminal leaflet often small/absent

comparison_matrix.microcarpa: shrub or small tree, often multi-stemmed
central and western Texas creek/riparian systems
comparison_matrix.major: more scattered west/central Texas canyon and stream populations

species_key: 1. Locate a mature fruit. If exceptionally small (~1.4–2.3 cm) with many narrow leaflets, check J. microcarpa; photograph mature nut for confirmation.
2. If intermediate fruit (~2–3.5 cm) and relatively broad/fewer leaflets, check J. major, especially a clean shell with deep grooves but relatively smooth surfaces between.
3. If large fruit (~3.5–8 cm), especially coarsely warty nut surface between deep grooves, check J. nigra; large-tree habit and deep furrowed bark support.

4. If fruit size, nut sculpture, and leaflet pattern contradict one another, record Juglans sp. or possible hybrid/intermediate. Do not force an ID: natural hybridization between Texas walnuts is documented.

visual_steps.name: One compound leaf, many leaflets
visual_steps.look_for: Find rachis attachment to twig; leaflets attach to rachis and are not separate leaves

visual_steps.name: Measure the whole fruit
visual_steps.look_for: Include ruler and entire green husk; tiny microcarpa to large nigra, major between

visual_steps.name: Remove or find a shed husk
visual_steps.look_for: Now distinguish the HARD nut shell grooves from soft outer husk texture

visual_steps.name: Check alternate twig and pith
visual_steps.look_for: Walnut has chambered pith; compare solid pith of Carya using an already fallen twig

photo_targets.requirement: Exact-species, rights-safe, same-scale shell photographs with groove and warty/smooth-between-grooves callouts
Ruler-scale fruit views, avoid immature fruit masquerading as mature size
Matched naturally fallen twig cuts, chambered versus solid interior
Whole compound leaf, alternate twig attachment and individual leaflet marked
